newsitem.title: FRANCE: Progress, but no deal on stability pact -- Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Progress, but no deal on stability pact -- Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday progress had been made in Franco-German talks on a stability pact to govern Europe's single currency, but no deal had been reached yet.

"We have made some progress, but we haven't finished," Waigel said after a meeting here with French President Jacques Chirac, new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin and French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn.
Waigel made no further comment as he emerged from the morning talks to take lunch, but smiled to reporters.

Waigel and Chancellor Helmut Kohl were holding their first meeting with French leaders since the left-wing government took power nearly two weeks ago, ushering in a period of so-called cohabitation with the conservative Chirac.

The new Jospin government has called for a commitment to fight unemployment to be worked into the stability pact, which is designed to enforce compliance with the Maastricht treaty's criteria on European economic and monetary union (EMU).

European leaders are racing against the clock to work out a compromise formula in time for the stability pact to be signed at next week's European Union summit in Amsterdam, at which a jobs chapter is also expected to be written at France's behest into a new treaty reforming EU institutions.
